players.product: MEMS timing (clocks/oscillators) for AI servers & optical modules

quarterly_data.signal: SiTime's 10-K names Robert Bosch LLC (Germany), TSMC and UMC (Taiwan) and Teledyne Digital Imaging Inc. (Canada) as its primary foundries and suppliers for its MEMS timing devices and analog mixed-signal circuit ICs, relying primarily on Bosch and Teledyne for MEMS fabrication and primarily on TSMC and UMC for analog circuits fabrication. Bosch fabricates SiTime's MEMS wafers based on purchase orders under a ten-year supply agreement whose initial term runs through February 2027 and renews automatically; other than Bosch, SiTime has no long-term supply agreements with most of its third-party manufacturing contractors. SiTime has in the past been impacted by industry-wide supply constraints affecting the supply of analog circuits manufactured by certain foundries, including TSMC, and affecting OSATs, which limited its ability to fully satisfy an increase in demand for some of its products. Packaging, assembly and test contractors include ASE (Taiwan), Carsem (Malaysia), UTAC (Thailand), Hana Semiconductor (Thailand), Daishinku (Japan) and STATS ChipPAC (Singapore).
quarterly_data.figure: Bosch MEMS wafer supply agreement: ten-year initial term through February 2027, renews automatically; TSMC and UMC primary analog-circuit foundries
